subjects.name: Data Structure
subjects.objective: This subject will help to understand fundamental concepts of data structure. Data structure has high significance in the field of Computer and IT. Association of information is urgent for usage and for that it requires proficient calculations. Comprehension of information structures and their related applications are profoundly expected to build practical program.
course_outcomes: Apply different data structures to solve real-life computational problems.
Demonstrate the need for data structures in efficient algorithm development.
Implement various sorting algorithms using appropriate data structures
Select and apply suitable data structures for given applications or scenarios

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Basics of Data Structure
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Data Structure , Data Representation, Data Types: Primitive and Non-Primitive, Algorithm, Time Complexity, Space complexity- Best case, Average case, Worst case

allSyllabusUnits.title: Array & Stack
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Study of Linear Data Structure, Representation of Array, Two- Dimensional Array, Multidimensional Array, Sparse Matrices , Application of Array, Introduction to Stack, Stack Operations: Push, Pop, Peep, Stack using Array, Applications of Stack , Polish Expression & Reverse Polish Expression

allSyllabusUnits.title: Queue & Link List
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Queue, Queue Operations: Insertion, Deletion, Types of Queue: Simple, Circular, Double ended queue(Deque) & Priority Queue, Applications of Queue, Introduction to Linked List , Memory Allocation, Operations: Creation, Insertion, Deletion, Types of Linked List & Applications

allSyllabusUnits.title: Tree And Graph
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Non-linear Data Structure , Introduction to Binary Tree, Tree Terminologies: Tree, Degree of a Node, Degree of a Tree, Level of a node, Leaf Node, Depth / Height of a Tree, In-Degree and Out- Degree, Path, Operations on Tree: Insert, Delete, Search, Height of Tree & Number of Nodes, Binary Tree Traversal: In-order, Pre- order, Post-order, Representation of Graphs, Graph Traversal: BFS (Breadth First Search), DFS(Depth First Search), Spanning Tree, Shortest Path, Minimum Spanning Tree

allSyllabusUnits.title: Sorting & Searching Techniques
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Sorting, Types of Sorting : Bubble Sort, Insertion Sort , Selection Sort, Merge Sort , Quick Sort, Introduction to Searching, Tyeps of Searching: Sequential Search, Binary Search

allSyllabusUnits.title: Hashing
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Hashing, Hash Table, Various Hash function : Division Method, Multiplication & Mid-square Method, Applications of Hashing Total Hours 42

firstHalfUnits.title: Introduction to Basics of Data Structure

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% by syllabus order/contact hours: Introduction to Basics of Data Structure; Array & Stack; Queue & Link List.

subjects.name: Database Management System
subjects.objective: A major rationale of a database system is to provide users with an intangible view of the data. That is, the system conceals certain details of how the information are put away and maintained. Thereby, data can be stored in compound data structures that permit competent retrieval, yet users see a basic and easy-to-use view of the data. The lowest level of abstraction, the physical level, depicts how the information is really put away and details the data structures.
course_outcomes: Apply techniques to identify business data issues and determine suitable requirements for resolving information-related problems.
Use appropriate methods to design and develop database systems that meet structural and performance requirements.
Apply data manipulation language (DML) commands to retrieve, modify, and manage data in a database.
Implement suitable physical storage and access methods to ensure efficient data retrieval and storage in database systems.
Apply normalization techniques to analyze and refine database schemas for improved data integrity and reduced redundancy.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Database Systems Data Models
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introducing the database and DBMS, Files and File Systems, Problems with File System and advantages of Database Management systems, The importance of Data models, Data Model Basic Building Blocks, Business Rules, Degree of Data Abstraction

allSyllabusUnits.title: Relational Data Model
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Structure of relational databases, Domains, Relations, Relational algebra, Relational algebra-Primary Operators, Relational algebra- syntax, Rrelational algebra queries

allSyllabusUnits.title: Entity Relationship Model
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Basic Entity ± Relationship Concepts: Entities, Relationship, Attributes, E ± R Diagram symbols, Conversion of Entity ± Relationship Model into Relations, Problems with Entity ± Relationship Models, Concepts: Specialisation and Generalisation

allSyllabusUnits.title: Relational Database Design
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Normalization of database tables: Database Tables and Normalization, The need for Normalization, The Normal forms:1NF , 2NF, The Normal form: 3NF , The Normal forms: BCNF , Denormalization

allSyllabusUnits.title: SQL Concepts
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to SQL : Data Definition Commands, Data Manipulation Commands, Select queries, Advanced Data Definition Commands, Advanced Select queries, Virtual Tables, Joining Database Tables Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% by syllabus order/contact hours: Database Systems Data Models; Relational Data Model; Entity Relationship Model.

subjects.name: Digital Electronics
subjects.objective: The subject aims to prepare the students,  To understand the basic of Digital Electronic concepts required in analysis and design of digital electronic circuits and systems.  To understand the number system, logic gates, Boolean algebra, etc.  To understand Construction and operation of various digital circuits such as Adder, Subtractor, Multiplexer, Demultiplexer, Decoder, Encoder, Flip-flops, Counters Registers.  To devolve the capability to Simplify, Analyze Various Digital Electronic Circuits.
course_outcomes: Perform conversion between various number systems.
Apply knowledge of Boolean algebra and other minimization techniques for digital circuit design.
Identify, formulate and solve a problem based on combinational and sequential circuits
Design various counters
Verify the functions of various digital integrated circuits.
Evaluate the specifications of logic families.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Module-1 Introduction
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Digital and Analog systems, logic level and pulse waveforms, elements of digital logic, Functions of digital logic

allSyllabusUnits.title: Module-2 Number systems and binary codes
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Number System: Binary number system, (addition, subtraction, multiplication, Division),, Octal and Hexadecimal Number system, Conversion from binary to decimal, octal and hexadecimal and vice versa,, Representation of Signed Numbers., Codes : BCD, XS-3, Gray Code ( with Conversion), Alphanumerical Code

allSyllabusUnits.title: Module-3 Logic Gates & Boolean Algebra
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Logic Gates: Positive and Negative logic, AND, OR , NOT, NAND, NOR, X-OR Gate, X-NOR Gate, Conversion from Universal Gate to all other Gates,, Boolean Algebra & Mapping Methods for Simplification:, Boolean Algebra, Karnaugh Maps, Realizing Logic Function with Gates.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Module-4 Combinational logic design
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Combinational Circuits and its implementations, Arithmetic Circuits - Adders and Subtractor,, BCD Adder, Look-Ahead Carry Generator, Multiplier, Magnitude comparator., Multiplexer and it¶s application, Encoders, Demultiplexers and Decoders and it¶s application, Generation and Checking, Code Conversion.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Module-5 Sequential circuits
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Flip-flops: Latch and Flip-flop, S-R flip-flops, D flip flop,, J-K flip flop, Application of flip flops, Registers: Classification , Serial in serial-out, serial-in parallel-out parallel- in serial-out and parallel- in parallel out shift register, Counters: Asynchronous (ripple) 4-bit binary counter, BCD Counter, Synchronous counters, UP/DOWN counter, Ring counters.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Module-6 Programmable Devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Programmable Logic Devices, Programmable Logic Arrays (PLA),, Programmable Array Logic (PAL).

firstHalfUnits.title: Module-2 Number systems and binary codes

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% by syllabus order/contact hours: Module-1 Introduction; Module-2 Number systems and binary codes; Module-3 Logic Gates & Boolean Algebra.

subjects.name: Mathematics-III
course_outcomes: Understand the order and selection of the objects using permutation and combination.
Understand and apply the basic concept of probability.
Expand the terms with higher degree using binomial theorem.
Differentiate the various function.
Learn the difference between scalar and vector, the properties of vectors and find the angle between them.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Permutation and Combination
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Basic permutation, Basic combination

allSyllabusUnits.title: Probability
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Classical probability, Compliment of event

allSyllabusUnits.title: Binomial Theorem
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Binomial theorem (without proof) for positive integral index (expansion and general form), Binomial theorem for any index (expansion without proof) first and second binomial approximation with applications to engineering problems

allSyllabusUnits.title: Differentiation
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition, Some properties, Derivative of some important functions, Chain rule, Derivative of implicit function, Derivative of parametric function, Logarithmic differentiation, Second order Derivative

allSyllabusUnits.title: Vectors
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Basic concept of Vector and Scalar, addition & subtraction, Product of Vectors, Geometric meaning of Scalar and Vector Product, Applications of Dot (scalar) and Cross (vector) product, Angle between two vectors Total Hours 28

subjects.name: Object Oriented Programming With C++
subjects.objective: The objective of this course is to enhance the programming abilities of students by introducing the fundamental concepts of Object-Oriented Programming using C++. It aims to help students understand classes and objects and apply these concepts to design and develop simple object-oriented applications.
course_outcomes: Apply the concepts of Object-Oriented Programming to differentiate procedural and object- oriented approaches in program design.
Use C++ programming constructs such as variables, control structures, namespaces and I/O operations to develop basic programs.
Implement functions, classes and objects in C++ programs using concepts like function overloading, inline functions and friend functions.
Apply constructors and destructors to initialize and manage objects in C++ applications.
Use inheritance concepts to design derived classes and demonstrate different types of inheritance.
Implement polymorphism, virtual functions and file handling techniques to develop object- oriented C++ applications.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to Object Oriented Concepts
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Concept of Object-Oriented Programming, Applications of Object- Oriented Programming, Characteristics of Object-Oriented Programming, Object-Oriented Programming vs Procedure Programming , Pros of OOP

allSyllabusUnits.title: Programming Basics
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to C++ programming, Basic structure of C++, Namespace , Directives, Using I/O Operators , Manipulators, Variables, Control Structure

allSyllabusUnits.title: Classes, Objects and Functions
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Class, Scope of class and accessing members of class, Class Object, Function Prototype , Function Calling, Call and return by reference, Inline functions , Default and const function arguments, Function overloading, Function overriding, Virtual Function, Friend Function

allSyllabusUnits.title: Constructor and Destructor
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Define Constructor, Types of Constructors: Default constructor, Parameterized constructor, Copy constructor, Dynamic Constructor Destructor

allSyllabusUnits.title: Inheritance
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Inheritance, Derived Class, Types of Inheritance: Single, Multi-level, Multiple, Hierarchical, Hybrid Inheritance, Abstract class and Virtual base class

allSyllabusUnits.title: Virtual Functions and polymorphism
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Concept of objects and pointers, this pointer, Virtual Functions, Pure Virtual Functions, Types of Polymorphism , Advantages of Polymorphism, Implementing polymorphism

allSyllabusUnits.title: Streams and File Management
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Concept of Stream, C++ Stream Classes, Formatted and unformatted I/O operations, File stream , C++ File stream classes, File management functions , File modes, Binary and random files , Exception handling Total Hours 42

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% by syllabus order/contact hours: Introduction to Object Oriented Concepts; Programming Basics; Classes, Objects and Functions; Constructor and Destructor.

subjects.name: Python Programming and Prompt Engineering
subjects.objective: In this course students will understand fundamentals of Python programming along with Generative AI and Prompt Engineering concepts. Students will learn basic programming principles and AI-assisted development techniques to meet modern computing requirements.
course_outcomes: Apply fundamental concepts of Python programming and basic AI concepts to solve simple computational problems.
Apply control structures and data structures in Python to develop logical programs.
Apply functions, modules, and file handling techniques to build structured Python applications.
Apply prompt engineering techniques to generate, refine, and debug Python code using AI tools.
Apply AI-assisted development methods and evaluation techniques to create reliable and ethical Python-based solutions.

allSyllabusUnits.title: INTRODUCTION TO PYTHON & AI FUNDAMENTALS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Programming, History and Features of Python, Structure of Python Program, Variables and Data Types, Operators, Input and Output Functions, Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Generative AI and Large Language Models (Concepts only), Overview of AI Tools for Programming Assistance

allSyllabusUnits.title: CONTROL FLOW AND DATA STRUCTURES IN PYTHON
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Decision Making Statements – if, if-else, elif ladder, Looping Statements – for loop, while loop, Nested loops, Lists – creation and operations, Tuples, Sets, Dictionaries – creation and access, String handling and built-in string functions.

allSyllabusUnits.title: FUNCTIONS, MODULES AND FILE HANDLING
allSyllabusUnits.topics: User-defined Functions, Function Arguments and Return Values, Recursion, Built-in Functions, Modules and Libraries, File Handling – Read and Write operations, Exception Handling – try, except, finally.

allSyllabusUnits.title: PROMPT ENGINEERING FUNDAMENTALS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Prompt Engineering, Structure of a Prompt – Instruction, Context, Constraints, Output Format, Role-based Prompts, Instruction Prompts, Few-shot Prompting, Prompt Templates for Code Generation and Debugging, Evaluating AI- generated Code – Accuracy, Clarity and Correctness

allSyllabusUnits.title: AI-ASSISTED PYTHON DEVELOPMENT & ETHICS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Using AI Tools for Code Generation, Code Debugging and Optimization, Prompt Chaining for Step-by-step Development, Detecting Hallucinations in AI-generated Code, Responsible AI Usage, Data Privacy and Security Considerations, Mini Project using Python and Prompt Engineering. Total Hours 0
